result: HeDNA recognition is required for DNA methylation maintenance but is dispensable for chromatin binding. The authors show that HeDNAmut UHRF1 cannot rescue DNA methylation loss in cells (similar to H3mut, RINGmut, and DNAmut), yet HeDNAmut retains chromatin binding ability, suggesting HeDNA recognition provides an additional regulatory layer beyond chromatin targeting.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly acknowledge this finding, stating 'they show that while HeDNA discrimination mutants of UHRF1 are unable to sustain methylation in vivo, they are able to associated with chromatin.' This result is central to the paper's novelty and is not questioned.

result: UHRF1 histone- and DNA-binding domains exhibit reciprocal positive allostery. The authors demonstrate that DNA (HeDNA, SyDNA, UnDNA) enhances UHRF1 binding to H3K9me3 peptides, and reciprocally, H3K9me3 peptide enhances DNA binding 5-10 fold irrespective of DNA methylation status. This cooperativity is dependent on the epigenetic signature on H3 and requires intact TTD-PHD multivalent engagement.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly state 'they provide evidence for positive allostery, showing that UHRF1 association with H3 is promoted by the presence of (He)DNA and visa versa.' The reviewers note this as a key difference from Fang et al., acknowledging 'reciprocal positive allostery between the histone- and DNA-binding domains of UHRF1' as a novel contribution.

result: DNA binding releases an intramolecular interaction between UHRF1 TTD-PHD and SRA-RING domains. Pull-down experiments show TTD-PHD associates with SRA-RING, and this interaction is disrupted by DNA (regardless of methylation status) but not by H3K9me2 peptide. The authors propose ligand-induced intramolecular rearrangement results in high-affinity chromatin retention through positive regulation of binding activities.
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge this mechanism, stating 'They provide a mechanism for this positive allostery, showing that the SRA and TTD-PHD domains normally associate with each other but that his interaction is abrogated in the presence of DNA, which presumably allows the free TTD-PHD domain to associate with its known chromatin target, H3K9me3.' This is accepted as part of the allosteric mechanism.

result: HeDNA specifically activates UHRF1 ubiquitylation of H3 substrates. The authors show robust H3 peptide ubiquitylation in the presence of HeDNA but not with SyDNA, UnDNA, or apo-UHRF1. HeDNA stimulated >100-fold rate enhancement of H3 mono-ubiquitylation compared to UnDNA, while auto-ubiquitylation showed only 2.5-fold enhancement. This substrate preference switch is also observed with mononucleosomes.
evaluation: Reviewers state 'they provide compelling evidence that the presence HeDNA stimulates the ubiquitylation activity of UHRF1 on H3 substrate' and acknowledge this as a major novel finding. The reviewers note this demonstrates 'HeDNA is an allosteric activator of UHRF1 expanding its lysine targets in histone H3' and represents sufficient novel insight 'particularly regarding ubiquitylation.'

result: HeDNA-dependent H3 ubiquitylation requires TTD-PHD substrate binding and multivalent H3K9me3 engagement. Excess H31-15K9me2 peptide (containing TTD-PHD binding site but not ubiquitin target lysines) inhibits mononucleosome ubiquitylation, while excess HeDNA does not. H3mut, Linkermut, DNAmut, and HeDNAmut all show defects in HeDNA-dependent H3 ubiquitylation.
evaluation: Reviewers accept these mechanistic details as part of the overall ubiquitylation activation story. The data supporting TTD-PHD's role in substrate recognition and the requirement for multivalent engagement are not questioned and support the main finding of HeDNA-dependent activation.

result: HeDNA activation does not occur through enhanced E2-ub binding or intrinsic discharge rate, but rather through altered substrate specificity. ITC and NMR show no change in E2-ub affinity with HeDNA. Ubiquitin discharge assays show only modest rate increase with HeDNA alone, but rapid H3 ubiquitylation when H3 peptide is present. The authors propose HeDNA serves as an allosteric switch directing TTD-PHD-bound H3 substrate to the E2-ub active site.
evaluation: This is the 'lysine prioritization' model that reviewers explicitly challenge as the 'weakest part of the manuscript.' Reviewer states: 'Looking at Figure 5D, I am not convinced that the presence of free lysine preferentially affects auto-ub over H3 peptide' and notes 'there is no prioritization of H3 lysines whatsoever.' The reviewer requests this line of argument be removed unless considerably improved evidence is provided. The mechanism of HeDNA activation remains incompletely explained.

result: Mass spectrometry identifies multiple H3 ubiquitylation sites enriched with HeDNA. In addition to H3K18 and H3K23, the authors identify H3K14ub, H3K27ub, and H3K36ub heavily enriched with HeDNA. H3K18ub is the most abundant site (>15-fold more than others), and H3K23ub only occurs with H3K18ub. HeDNA also alters UHRF1 auto-ubiquitylation sites, including 9-fold enrichment of K303ub.
evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge the mass spectrometry work as part of the comprehensive analysis, stating the authors 'use mass spectroscopy techniques to determine the PTMs associated with HeDNA simulated UHRF1 activity on nucleosomes.' This identification of multiple ubiquitylation sites is accepted as supporting the allosteric activation model.

result: H3K9 methylation directs UHRF1 ubiquitylation to adjacent lysines in the presence of HeDNA. Mass spectrometry shows all three H3K9 methylation states co-occur with ubiquitylated peptides. Immunoblotting confirms ubiquitylated H3 is detected with HeDNA on H3K9me3-marked nucleosomes but not on H3K9acK14ac-marked nucleosomes. Titration experiments show H3K9me2 protein is modified at lower concentrations than unmodified H3.
evaluation: Reviewers describe this as 'a detailed biochemical and proteomic analysis of the role of H3K9me3 and hemi-methylated DNA on the functions of the UHRF1 ubiquitin ligase.' The connection between H3K9 methylation and ubiquitylation targeting is accepted as part of the comprehensive characterization.

result: Model: UHRF1 is targeted to chromatin through coordinated histone and DNA reading activities via reciprocal positive allostery, and HeDNA recognition activates H3 ubiquitylation to recruit DNMT1. HeDNA sensing is not required for bulk chromatin targeting but provides regulatory specificity. The avidity from sub-μM affinities for both DNA and H3 through positive allostery provides the biochemical basis for exclusive chromatin localization.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly endorse the conceptual advance: 'In general the chromatin field considers protein interactions with epigenetic marks to be the basis for recruitment of chromatin modifiers. This study clearly indicates allosteric activation of chromatin modifiers needs to also be considered.' The model integrating chromatin targeting and allosteric activation is accepted.

result: Proposed structural mechanism: HeDNA binding positions the RING in proximity to H3 binding region, while SyDNA/UnDNA binding conformationally restricts RING activity. The NKR finger adopts a highly ordered conformation upon HeDNA binding, which may be critical for H3 ubiquitylation activation.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 states: 'In my view the most important aspect of this paper is to establish the mechanism through which HeDNA binding stimulates ubiquitylation' but notes 'we are left, somewhat disappointingly, with the speculation that HeDNA binding causes specific conformational changes that reposition the RING domain.' The structural mechanism remains speculative and incompletely resolved.
